 versus  STATE (NCT OF DELHI)

 CORAM:
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GIRISH KATHPALIA  OR  % 16
1. Heard.

2. By way of this application under Section 438 Cr.P.C., the applicant/ accused (husband of complainant de facto) seeks grant of anticipatory bail in the case FIR No. 1051/2022 registered at P.S. Paschim Vihar West for offences under Sections 498A/406/377/506/34 of the IPC.
3. As informed by both the sides, parents and other relatives of the accused/applicant are not sought to be arrested at this stage.
4. I have also heard the complainant de facto as well as her counsel keeping in mind the nature of allegations in the FIR.

The offence under Section 377 IPC, being the most serious allegation, learned counsel for both sides were asked to take me through the FIR and it was found that the only expression pertaining to the said offence is two words: "aparakratik maithun".

Apart from the same,
there is no other averment qua the said offence under Section 377 IPC.

Even during the arguments,
neither the This is a digitally signed order.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that offence of Section 377 of the IPC has been added in the FIR simply to circumvent the legal position, as laid down in various judicial precedents including the case of Arnesh Kumar vs State of Bihar, (2014) 8 SCC 273.
6.

sentences.text: As per prosecution and the complainant de facto, the applicant/accused has not returned the complete istridhan jewellery, which was gifted at the time of marriage.
As per learned counsel for applicant/accused, the said jewellery was gifted to the relatives of applicant/accused, therefore he could not return the same.

At the same time, learned counsel for the applicant/accused refers to the judgments in the cases of Puran Singh vs State of Delhi, 2021:DHC:4116 and Chetan Kapoor @ Vikas vs State,
2015:DHC:7600DB to buttress his contention that the Court while dealing with bail applications does not function as a recovery forum as regards the jewellery articles.

sentences.text: 8. As mentioned above, I specifically heard the complainant de facto as well as her counsel and their only grievance is that the complete jewellery articles have not been returned by the applicant/accused.
9. As informed by both the sides, the complainant de facto got married with the applicant/accused on 14.02.2020 and it was a love marriage.
From 11.01.2022, they have been living separately from each other.
The FIR in question was registered on 30.12.2022.

Learned counsel for the applicant/accused specifically submitted that in response to his notice under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, the complainant de facto did not even whisper any allegation related to the offence under Section 377 IPC.
There This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 17/10/2023 at 22:45:34 is also no denial from the side of the complainant de facto that the applicant/accused has been paying her a sum of Rs. 10,000/- per month towards maintenance and that he bore hospital expenses for delivery of the child of the parties.
10. In response to a specific query, the complainant de facto stated that she does not wish to live with the applicant/accused.
But, she also stated that till date she has not initiated any divorce proceedings.
Parties have a child aged about 01 year and is in custody of the complainant de facto.

In such circumstances, denying protection and sending the accused/applicant to jail at this stage would throttle not just the matrimony but also the same would not be in the welfare of the child.
11.
Considering the above circumstances, the application is allowed.

In the event of his arrest, the applicant/accused be released on bail subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.
20,000/- with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer/Arresting Officer/SHO concerned.
The applicant/accused shall cooperate with the investigating agency.
It is expected that both sides would take all possible steps to resolve their matrimonial dispute in the larger interest of the child.
As requested, copy of this order be given dasti.
GIRISH KATHPALIA, J OCTOBER 16, 2023/
